title: Famicom Detective Club
subtitle: Two early mysteries return in a new form
summary: Famicom Detective Club's Switch remakes bring The Missing Heir and The Girl Who Stands Behind to a new audience, released on 14 May 2021.
body: Famicom Detective Club's Switch remakes bring The Missing Heir and The Girl Who Stands Behind to a new audience, released on 14 May 2021. Originally written for the Famicom Disk System in 1988 and 1989, the two adventures follow a young investigator through murders and unsettling local stories. Mages rebuilt their presentation with illustrated scenes and performances. The player advances through conversations and examination, gradually connecting an apparent supernatural threat to the people and events that can be investigated within each community.

Commands such as asking, examining, showing an item and moving to another location structure the inquiry. Looking closely at a scene can reveal an object or a reason to return to a conversation. Progress often comes from reconsidering a subject after another discovery changes its meaning. The Missing Heir begins with the investigator suffering memory loss while examining a death in the Ayashiro family. The Girl Who Stands Behind returns to an earlier case, giving the pair a shared cast but a different point in the investigator's life.

Yoshio Sakamoto's original writing drew on detective fiction, horror cinema and the command-based Japanese adventure tradition. The 2021 editions made the stories officially available outside Japan for the first time, with Takeshi Abo contributing the remakes' music. They preserve the act of assembling a case through repeated attention to testimony and detail while changing how its people and places are presented. That return also renewed the series itself, leading eventually to a completely new investigation in Emio – The Smiling Man.
